name: Surface Code Quantum Error Correction Below Threshold
description: Memory benchmark demonstrating a quantum error-correcting code operating below the fault-tolerant threshold on a superconducting processor. Google's team ran distance-3, -5 and -7 surface codes and showed that logical error rate per cycle drops by a factor Lambda each time code distance is increased by two, proving exponential error suppression with scale. Also ran a distance-29 repetition code. The distance-7 logical memory outlived its best physical qubit by a factor of 2.4, a first-of-its-kind result for superconducting hardware.
significance: First demonstration on superconducting hardware that increasing code distance reduces logical error exponentially — crossing the practical break-even point required for scalable fault-tolerant quantum computation.

news.title: IBM and UChicago Achieve Logical Error Rates 10× Below Physical in 70-Logical-Qubit Encoded Circuits
news.excerpt: IBM and UChicago ran 70 logical qubits with effective logical error rates 10× lower than physical qubit error rates, completing 2,415 logical two-qubit gates and 468 T gates. Results are released openly on the IBM Quantum Advantage Tracker.
